_comment: Fictitious answer library and RFP questions for `arp rfp golden drafts` (AC-43, AC-44). An answerable question is fully answered by the library; an unanswerable one is not answered by it at all.

library.question: Describe your firm.
library.answer: Northwind Capital Partners is an independent, employee-owned asset manager founded in 2009 and based in Edinburgh.

library.question: What is your total AUM?
library.answer: Northwind manages GBP 8.2bn as of 30 June 2026.

library.question: How many investment professionals do you employ?
library.answer: We employ 34 investment professionals out of 61 staff.

library.question: Are you a PRI signatory?
library.answer: Yes. Northwind has been a signatory to the UN Principles for Responsible Investment since 2011.

library.question: Describe your ESG integration.
library.answer: ESG factors are scored for every holding by the analyst who covers it, and the scores feed the position sizing of each portfolio.

library.question: Do you use derivatives?
library.answer: We use currency forwards for hedging only. We do not use derivatives for leverage.

library.question: Describe your voting policy.
library.answer: We vote at every meeting of every holding, following our published voting policy, and publish our votes quarterly.

library.question: Who is your custodian?
library.answer: Our custodian for segregated mandates is Harbour Trust Bank.

library.question: How often do you report to clients?
library.answer: Clients receive monthly performance reports and a quarterly investment and stewardship report.

library.question: What is your fee for segregated mandates?
library.answer: The fee for a segregated global equity mandate is 0.45% per year on the first GBP 100m and 0.35% above that.

library.question: Describe your business continuity plan.
library.answer: Our business continuity plan is tested twice a year, and all staff can work fully remotely from a secondary site.

library.question: Who owns the firm?
library.answer: The firm is wholly owned by its employees; no single employee holds more than 15% of the shares.
